coverage.reason: The feature backfill issues own the current shipped-feature inventory and must switch this registry to complete mode after their entries land.

features.title: Typed BGM routing, variants, selectors, and continuation

cases.title: Tester-case catalog foundation
profiles: Clean source checkout with Python 3; no ROM, emulator, artifact, or optional feature profile
cases.purpose: Exercise the stable catalog schema and checker integration that future feature cases extend.
cases.prerequisites: Start from the repository root with docs/test-cases and scripts/check_docs.py present; no save state is needed.
cases.actions: Inspect the catalog index, template, and registry; run the focused docs-checker unit test and the checker command named below.
cases.expected_result: The registry exposes separate feature and case records, the procedure is indexed, and both commands accept the valid foundation data.
cases.negative_control: Focused fixtures reject malformed or duplicate IDs, unknown ownership, missing links or anchors, placeholders, unnamed automation, missing exclusion rationale, and a missing complete-mode feature.
cases.interactions: Depends on issue #53's tester-case contract. The feature backfill is deliberately deferred to issues #55 through #58.
cases.save_compatibility: No save bytes, migration, compatibility epoch, or runtime profile changes.
cases.limitations: This foundation validates the schema and extension seam only; it does not yet assert full current-feature coverage.

cases.title: Resolve ordered portrait and minimug rules
profiles: Default modern source checkout with a host C compiler; no ROM, save, or replacement portrait assets
cases.purpose: Prove declaration-order, selector, flag, full-portrait, and minimug resolution through a disposable native fixture.
cases.prerequisites: Keep the committed production registry empty; the test creates and deletes its fixture under build/test-artifacts.
cases.actions: Run the named resolver unittest and inspect its ordered character/class/chapter/flag fixture assertions.
cases.expected_result: The real resolver selects the first valid matching full/minimug row and preserves the committed empty registry.
cases.negative_control: Conflicting flags and an out-of-range full portrait ID do not select a fixture row.
cases.interactions: No optional profile dependency or conflict; resolves existing IDs only and does not add art.
cases.save_compatibility: Read-only resolver; no save bytes, migration, or compatibility epoch change.
cases.limitations: The fixture proves framework resolution, not a project-authored campaign portrait mapping.

cases.title: Fall back for empty or invalid portrait registries
profiles: Default modern source checkout with a host C compiler; no ROM or saved state
cases.purpose: Prove empty and invalid registry fallback plus chapter-specific legacy portrait substitution.
cases.prerequisites: Use the committed empty registry and the temporary invalid-bound row from the native resolver fixture.
cases.actions: Run the named resolver unittest and inspect the invalid-ID, minimug fallback, and chapter 0x22 assertions.
cases.expected_result: Legacy character/class/minimug behavior remains available when no valid custom row can apply.
cases.negative_control: An invalid registry cannot partially apply an earlier row or bypass legacy fallback.
cases.interactions: Preserves existing chapter substitutions and has no locale, resource, or feature-profile interaction.
cases.save_compatibility: No save state is read or written.
cases.cleanup: The unittest deletes its native fixture directory.
cases.limitations: The stock campaign deliberately contains no custom portrait registry rows.

cases.title: Persist expanded sound-room unlocks safely
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3; no ROM or real SRAM image
cases.purpose: Prove 256-slot sound-room persistence, visibility/playability state, migration, and corruption rejection.
cases.prerequisites: Start without a save file; the test builds every 0x24-byte record in memory.
cases.actions: Run the named sound-room unittest and inspect synthetic legacy/current/corrupt record outcomes.
cases.expected_result: IDs through 255 persist losslessly, visibility stays separate from playability, and current migration is idempotent.
cases.negative_control: Out-of-range IDs, bad checksums, and unknown format markers are rejected without a guessed write.
cases.interactions: Sound-room data is independent of locale, casual markers, and ExpansionUserPrefs.
cases.save_compatibility: The record stays at SRAM 0x7224 with size 0x24 and its existing checksum domain.
cases.cleanup: All synthetic records are in memory and vanish on test exit.
cases.limitations: No project-specific catalog condition or song is shipped by this framework case.

cases.title: Keep an empty BGM registry inert and honor explicit requests
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3 and a host C compiler; preserve continuation policy
cases.purpose: Prove empty-registry fallback and authoritative explicit BGM routing using a disposable native fixture.
cases.prerequisites: Keep src/data/bgm_registry.json empty; do not add rows outside the test fixture.
cases.actions: Run the named BGM unittest and make bgm-registry-check, then inspect ordinary and explicit request assertions.
cases.expected_result: Empty production data retains legacy songs while an explicit request wins and SONG_NONE remains a stop.
cases.negative_control: A matching fixture row cannot replace an explicit song or make the committed empty registry select music.
cases.interactions: No sound-room persistence dependency; continuation policy is separately exercised by TC-BGM-004.
cases.save_compatibility: Routing and continuation do not change save data.
cases.limitations: The fixture proves route selection, not subjective music quality or campaign content.

cases.title: Select chapter and flag variants deterministically
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3 and a host C compiler
cases.purpose: Prove variant priority/source-order selection and legal flag/mask boundaries in a disposable fixture.
cases.prerequisites: Use the native test fixture; leave the committed BGM registry empty.
cases.actions: Run the named BGM unittest and observe its chapter-7, flag-5, equal-priority source-order fixture.
cases.expected_result: The matching high-priority variant wins and equal priorities retain declaration order.
cases.negative_control: Sentinel, out-of-space flag, chapter, context, and song values fail validation before generation.
cases.interactions: Ordinary fallback routing only; explicit requests remain authoritative.
cases.save_compatibility: Variant records do not persist or change the save format.
cases.cleanup: The unittest removes its generated native probe.
cases.limitations: The empty production registry intentionally has no campaign-authored variant.

cases.title: Resolve dancer and staff selectors by specificity
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3 and a host C compiler
cases.purpose: Prove action selector priority, specificity, source order, and legacy fallback with a disposable fixture.
cases.prerequisites: Use the in-test selector fixture and no production registry rows.
cases.actions: Run the named BGM unittest and inspect generic/specific dancer plus staff-kind/item selection outcomes.
cases.expected_result: Priority then specificity then source order select a song; no matching staff selector preserves legacy audio.
cases.negative_control: Invalid actions, staff-none calls, and invalid selector IDs cannot select a custom song.
cases.interactions: Independent of sound-room and continuation persistence; it consumes ordinary action fallback only.
cases.save_compatibility: No action selector state is saved.
cases.cleanup: The unittest deletes its native artifact directory.
cases.limitations: The test verifies routing semantics only; the stock registry is intentionally empty.

cases.title: Apply continuation policy and preserve stop requests
profiles: Modern debug source profile with preserve, resume, or restart continuation policy
cases.purpose: Prove the three configured continuation paths and SONG_NONE stop behavior.
cases.prerequisites: Use a clean source profile and configure one documented continuation policy at a time.
cases.actions: Run the named BGM unittest and invoke expansion_config.py resolve for preserve, resume, and restart.
cases.expected_result: Preserve, resume, and restart take their distinct documented continuation branches and valid choices affect identity.
cases.negative_control: Invalid policy text fails configuration resolution and SONG_NONE bypasses routing.
cases.interactions: Composes with ordinary variants/selectors and has no sound-room save dependency.
cases.save_compatibility: Policy changes configuration identity only, never save compatibility.
cases.cleanup: Remove local configure outputs only if configure was run.
cases.limitations: The deterministic case asserts control flow rather than whether a listener prefers a transition.

automation.command: python3 scripts/modernize/expansion_config.py resolve --config debug --abi aapcs --rom-size 16M --bgm-continuation-policy preserve

cases.title: Apply standard, reduced, and off battle presentation
profiles: Default modern source checkout with a host C compiler; no ROM or save
cases.purpose: Prove semantic standard, reduced, and off number/effect policy behavior.
cases.prerequisites: No fixture or game state is required; the native probe owns its removable artifact directory.
cases.actions: Run the named native policy unittest and inspect standard, reduced, and off assertions.
cases.expected_result: Standard retains effects/numbers, reduced retains damage only with bounded timing, and off suppresses all numbers/effects.
cases.negative_control: The existing default Animation option remains standard and unsupported values do not select a new effect.
cases.interactions: The existing Animation setting persists normally; utility preference selection is covered by TC-UTILITY-001.
cases.save_compatibility: No save layout change; existing Animation persistence remains in its original record.
cases.limitations: Semantic suppression is automated; no subjective visual preference is a pass criterion.

cases.title: Reject invalid presentation resources and persist selections
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3 and a host C compiler
cases.purpose: Prove bounded policy validation and saved preference selection normalization.
cases.prerequisites: No SRAM image is required; tests construct synthetic preference records.
cases.actions: Run the named policy, UI registry, and native preference unittests.
cases.expected_result: Only bounded resources/timings validate, and valid policy selections round-trip through existing preferences.
cases.negative_control: Out-of-range policy resources, unknown policies, unsupported extension bytes, and out-of-mask utility bits are rejected.
cases.interactions: Shares ExpansionUserPrefs with locale selection but does not affect sound-room or casual records.
cases.save_compatibility: Uses the fixed checksummed 12-byte preference record without offset or epoch changes.
cases.cleanup: All probe artifacts are deleted by the tests.
cases.limitations: Metadata validation does not reserve GPU resources.

cases.title: Resolve localized presentation manifest fallbacks safely
profiles: Default modern source checkout with Python 3 and a host C compiler; no custom assets or save
cases.purpose: Prove generated manifest title fallback, escaping, resource validation, and record capacity.
cases.prerequisites: Use the committed ui_presentation.json; schema tests clone records and clean their generated artifacts.
cases.actions: Run the named schema unittest and make generated-data-check.
cases.expected_result: Localized keys and deterministic static fallback text validate within the 32-record/resource bounds.
cases.negative_control: Missing required assets, unknown keys, NUL text, resource overflow, and record 33 fail before output.
cases.interactions: Generated presentation data leaves default rendering and locale persistence unchanged until a project calls the resolver seam.
cases.limitations: The case proves data/resolver inputs, not a project-specific screen or asset package.

cases.title: Persist available utility preferences without record interference
profiles: Default modern source checkout and EXPANSION_DANGER_OVERLAY_MENU=1 opt-in profile; Python 3 and a host C compiler
cases.purpose: Prove descriptor availability, preference persistence, safe legacy/unknown defaults, and record isolation.
cases.prerequisites: Use synthetic ExpansionUserPrefs records; start with Threat Range unavailable in the default profile.
cases.actions: Run the named UI/native tests and resolve both danger-overlay-menu profile values with expansion_config.py.
cases.expected_result: Battle presentation is available, Threat Range is profile-gated, and valid selections persist without corrupting other records.
cases.negative_control: Unknown policies, out-of-mask bits, newer schemas, and unavailable Threat Range safely reject or default.
cases.interactions: Uses the one descriptor registry and existing map-menu command; does not add a second settings screen.
cases.save_compatibility: Reuses the fixed 12-byte preference record and does not reuse sound-room or casual bytes.
cases.cleanup: No persistent fixture, ROM, or save is created.
cases.limitations: The catalog remains foundation mode and the case does not score subjective UX preference.
